svg.text: A goal's measures are its own sub-items and have no
page of their own: they are already on the Goals view,
read with the goals. This process acts on what is there.
An archived measure is listed under the goal it belongs
to, in the Goals archive. Reading it, bringing it back and
destroying it are their own process (BP15).
The check-in history hangs on the measure's identity,
A measure takes its own check-in history with it and
brings it back with it. A project parented on it keeps its
Its check-in history goes with it, unasked, and nothing
else does, so there is nothing to disclose and nothing to
approve: a project parented on it survives minus the link.
Numeric carries a start value, a target, a unit and a
direction, and its current value starts at the start value;
boolean carries done and not done, starting at not done.
The type is editable like the start value, the target and
the unit, and the recorded check-ins are left as they
Numeric takes the value the current value moves to.
Boolean takes done and not done. A note is optional
either way. Nothing is read first: the measure and where
it stands arrived with the goals.
Its check-in history goes with it and comes back with it,
into a live goal. While it is away it is frozen, so nothing is
The history is append-only, so a date that already carries
a check-in takes another and each is its own data point.
The current value is what the latest one says, and the
start value until there is one. A check-in records a data
There is no untyped measure. The type is editable like
the start value, the target and the unit, and the check-ins
already recorded are left as they stand, each in the type
